# aarambh-studio v4.0.0

aarambh-studio v4.0.0 is the fourth — and **final planned** — production
source release of the ground-up Rust LLM application. It completes the v4 arc
(Phases 41–55) on top of the completed v3.0.0 base and reaches a
deliberately-declared end state for the project. No v5 roadmap exists as of
this release.

## Distribution Policy

- This is a GitHub source release of an application, not a crates.io library
  release. This corrects and finalises the policy implied by v3 §40 —
  aarambh-studio is an **application**, not a **library**, and the confirmed
  policy going forward is: source only, no crates.io publish, ever, consistent
  with v1.0.0's and v2.0.0's original release policy.
- All 21 workspace packages remain `publish = false`.
- GitHub's automatic source archives are the only release assets.
- No pretrained checkpoint, adapter, tokenizer, optimizer state, SafeTensors,
  GGUF file, or compiled CPU/CUDA binary is included.
- Users train, convert, fine-tune, quantise, and serve their own local
  checkpoints.

## v4 Highlights

### Efficient Attention Family Finished (Phases 41, 29–30, v3 §27)

- **Multi-Head Latent Attention (MLA)** — the third attention kind, after
  standard scaled dot-product (v1) and Gated DeltaNet / DeepSeek Sparse
  Attention (v3). Latent KV compression down-projects keys/values into a
  shared latent vector before the cache, materially cutting KV memory for
  long contexts. Retrofittable onto existing checkpoints via continued
  pretraining; the KV-cache report (`eval --kv-cache-report`) quantifies the
  saving per layer.
- Combined: the v4.0 attention stack is a complete family — full attention,
  Gated DeltaNet, DSA, and MLA — selectable per-layer via TOML, with dense
  fallback retained for correctness-first configurations.

### Audio Modality (Phase 42)

- A frozen audio spectrogram transformer + trainable projector, parallel to
  the vision path. Pure-Rust WAV PCM decode + mel-spectrogram extraction (no
  FFmpeg / no MP3/FLAC/Ogg — WAV PCM only, an explicit honesty boundary).
- New reserved `<audio>` token fusion; audio DoRA/QDoRA tuning shares the
  single VLM training code path. Audio-QA eval task included.

### Sparse/Grouped MoE Dispatch (Phase 43)

- Resolves v2/v3's deferred optimisation: real sparse dispatch on CUDA
  (only the selected experts' rows touched), with the dense masked-matmul
  path retained on CPU for correctness-first portability. Equivalence proven
  by a per-layer dense-vs-sparse numerical test.

### Multi-Node Distributed Training (Phase 44)

- Data-parallel training across nodes via TCP rendezvous with a single-retry
  fault policy. Not model/pipeline-parallel (an explicit out-of-scope). The
  existing single-node NCCL path from v2 remains the default for single-host
  GPU training.

### Test-Time Compute Scaling (Phase 45)

- Best-of-N sampling, self-consistency (majority vote over N samples),
  verifier-based selection, and a heuristic process-reward scorer (plus a
  trait for a future trained head). Text-only; ships a heuristic, not a
  trained reward model.

### RLAIF (Phase 46)

- A third alignment signal: a judge model scores preference pairs, feeding
  the existing DPO pipeline. Kept deliberately separate from the online
  self-learning loop (same framing as model merging — offline, measured, not
  assumed improved).

### Sandboxed Tool Execution (Phase 47)

- Opt-in (`agent --execute-tools`) execution of operator-authorised,
  closed-world named capabilities (e.g. `read_file_in_workdir`) inside a
  bounded envelope. A general-purpose code-execution sandbox remains out of
  scope — execution is strictly closed-world, never arbitrary code or shell.

### Multi-Agent Orchestration (Phase 48)

- One top-level orchestrating reasoning process delegates independent
  sub-tasks to multiple parallel sandboxed tool-execution sub-chains, then
  merges results back into its own context via the existing `ToolResult`
  ingestion path applied recursively. Three hard, operator-set bounds: max
  sub-agent count, max total execution time budget, and sandbox scope
  containment (`AuthorizationScope::intersect` — a sub-agent's scope is only
  ever a subset of its orchestrator's). Sub-chains run sequentially by
  default (CPU-first honest; true parallelism would require a `Send + Sync`
  `ChainDecoder`, out of scope for the source release).

### Retrieval-Augmented Generation (Phase 49)

- A from-scratch, pure-Rust retrieval pipeline (new `aarambh-studio-retrieve`
  crate): chunking, embedding heads, a navigable small-world graph ANN index,
  and prompt augmentation before generation — no external vector database
  dependency for the core index. The default tested embedder is weight-free
  (hashing) so the whole pipeline runs without a trained embedding checkpoint.

### Model Merging / Weight Averaging (Phase 50)

- A from-scratch, pure-Rust merging toolkit (new `merge.rs` module in the
  existing `aarambh-studio-weights` crate, no new crate, no new external
  dependency): five standard algorithms — linear/Model-Soups, SLERP,
  task-vector arithmetic, TIES-Merging, and DARE. Hard shape/schema validation
  before any write; CPU-first f32 math; quality measured by `eval`, never
  assumed improved.

### Public Inference Server + Prefix Caching (Phase 51)

- The existing `aarambh-studio-serve` server gains opt-in multi-tenant
  API-key auth, per-key rate limiting (RPM + TPM), per-tenant in-flight
  isolation, and prompt-prefix KV caching (longest-prefix reuse with LRU
  eviction under a configurable memory ceiling). All opt-in; the loopback-only,
  unauthenticated single-user mode from v2 §31 remains the default. Still
  self-hosted — no billing, no auto-scaling.

### System Role, Chat-Template Versioning, Context Management (Phase 52)

- A documented, first-class system role marker (`SYSTEM`, reserved token id 17
  — the next free id; id 7 has been `IMAGE` since v2.0.0 and is never
  reassigned, per the project's append-never-reassign discipline). A
  `chat_template_version` tag on tokenizer config and checkpoint metadata with a
  fail-loud startup mismatch gate. A unified `ContextTruncationPolicy`
  (SlidingWindow / Summarize / Reject) referenced by every long-context
  feature. A canonical `docs/SAMPLING_DEFAULTS.md` reference.

### Red-Team / Adversarial Safety Evaluation (Phase 53)

- A single systematic, end-to-end adversarial-testing pass run once, near the
  end of v4.0, against the complete v4.0 attack surface: the safety layer and
  system-turn precedence, the closed-world sandboxed tool-execution boundary,
  the orchestrator hard bounds, and the public-server auth / rate-limit /
  tenant-isolation surface. A 24-case corpus (hand-authored / free-public-sourced
  only) carries a labelled expected outcome per case; a failing case is surfaced
  plainly in the report, never silently dropped. New `redteam/` module tree +
  `eval --redteam` CLI flag; runs without a trained model.

### Model Card & Release Documentation Standard (Phase 54)

- One canonical, **assembled** (not hand-written) document per released
  checkpoint configuration, summarising intended use, capabilities, known
  limitations, training-data provenance, eval-harness scores, and red-team
  findings. Generated from an eval-harness scorecard + the red-team report +
  static metadata, so it cannot silently drift out of sync with actual eval
  numbers. New `model_card.rs` module + `eval --generate-model-card` CLI flag.
  Generation fails loudly if no red-team report is present or the report is
  not clean — a checkpoint cannot get a model card without a clean red-team
  pass.

### Final Source Release (Phase 55)

- Every workspace package inherits version `4.0.0`; `Cargo.lock` committed;
  all release commands use `--locked`. The release audit is extended to cover
  every v4 crate surface (gates `ROADMAP_V4.md` for unchecked tasks and asserts
  the presence of the audio/retrieve/agent/serve crates). Documentation
  (`ARCHITECTURE_V4.md`, `ROADMAP_V4.md`, `SELF_LEARNING_V4.md`, `CHANGELOG.md`,
  `README.md`) finalised with the full v1 → v4 arc. v4.0.0 is declared the
  final planned version — no v5 roadmap exists as of this release.

## Production Hardening

- Every package reports version `4.0.0`; `aarambh-studio --version` matches
  the tag.
- Rust 1.89 is the MSRV.
- `Cargo.lock` is committed and all CI/release commands use `--locked`.
- The release profile uses `opt-level=3`, Thin LTO, one codegen unit, and
  stripped debug info.
- Every exported Rust API is documented and `missing_docs` is denied.
- Every unsafe block has an explicit safety rationale and Clippy enforces it.
- The release audit rejects unfinished implementation markers, unchecked
  roadmap tasks (including `ROADMAP_V4.md`), publishable packages, version
  drift, empty CUDA kernel bodies, tracked model artifacts, and `cargo publish`
  in workflows.
- CI validates stable Rust, Rust 1.89, formatting, checks, Clippy, tests,
  rustdoc, release build, CLI coverage, shell syntax, and RustSec advisories.
- CI now also covers the `aarambh-studio-audio`, `aarambh-studio-retrieve`
  crates, the extended `aarambh-studio-agent` and `aarambh-studio-serve`
  surfaces, and the `eval --redteam` / `eval --generate-model-card` CLI flags.

## Install From Source

```sh
git clone https://github.com/AarambhDevHub/aarambh-studio.git
cd aarambh-studio
git checkout v4.0.0
cargo build --release -p aarambh-studio --locked
target/release/aarambh-studio --version
```

For a local Cargo installation from the checked-out source:

```sh
cargo install --path aarambh-studio --locked
aarambh-studio --version
```

## Compatibility

- Existing v1/v2/v3 dense model configurations remain valid when v4-only
  fields (`mla`, `audio`, `sparse_moe`, `multinode`, `test_time`, `rlaif`,
  `sandbox`, `orchestrate`, `rag`, `merge`, `system_role`,
  `chat_template_version`, `context_policy`, `redteam`, `model_card`) are
  absent — each defaults off.
- Existing v1/v2/v3 tokenizer IDs and checkpoint paths remain supported.
- Existing LoRA/DoRA/QAT/MTP/DeltaNet/DSA paths remain available.
- v4.0.x is the final supported release line; v3.0.x is no longer maintained.

## Known Boundaries

- No pretrained model quality claim is made because no weights are distributed.
- No crate is published to crates.io — v4.0.0 is a source-only release.
- MoE uses dense masked dispatch on CPU (sparse dispatch is CUDA-only).
- Multi-node training is data-parallel only, not model/pipeline-parallel, with
  a single-retry fault policy.
- Test-time compute scaling is text-only and ships a heuristic
  process-reward scorer plus a trait for a future trained head.
- Tool execution is strictly closed-world, named-capability — never arbitrary
  code or shell execution.
- Multi-agent sub-chains run sequentially by default (CPU-first honest).
- RAG's core index is the from-scratch pure-Rust navigable small-world graph;
  no external vector database is permitted for the core index.
- Video is visual-only H.264 MP4; audio is WAV PCM only (no MP3/FLAC/Ogg);
  documents are pixel-based (no OCR/table parser).
- The server is local/single-model by default; Phase 51 makes public
  multi-tenant self-hosting possible, not a hosted product — no billing, no
  auto-scaling.
- CUDA throughput depends on the GPU, driver, toolkit, shape, and dtype;
  hardware timing is not a CI gate.

## Security

- Streaming and non-streaming requests pass through the configured safety policy.
- Non-loopback server binds require bearer authentication; opt-in multi-tenant
  mode adds per-key rate limits (RPM + TPM) and per-tenant in-flight isolation.
- Request bodies and queues are bounded, CORS is opt-in, and internal errors
  are sanitized.
- Safety audit logs store prompt hashes rather than raw prompts.
- Sandboxed tool execution enforces a closed-world allowlist; orchestrator
  sub-agents inherit only a subset of their parent's authorisation scope.
- A clean red-team report is required before a model card can be assembled.

See `CHANGELOG.md`, `ARCHITECTURE_V4.md`, `ROADMAP_V4.md`, `SELF_LEARNING_V4.md`,
and `RELEASE.md` for the complete engineering history and release procedure.

---

**v4.0.0 is the final planned version of aarambh-studio.** The project's
roadmap arc — from v1's foundational pipeline, through v2's first growth
phase, v3's second growth phase, to v4's completion phase — reaches a natural,
deliberately-declared end state here. Not every software project needs an
indefinitely-growing roadmap.
